key_insight: Ensembling variational quantum regressors improves nonlinear function prediction, with sequential AdaBoost achieving significantly better accuracy than independently trained Bagging.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a way to combine imperfect quantum regressors for nonlinear modeling without requiring fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
method: Train variational quantum regressors independently with Bagging or sequentially with AdaBoost.
Select features from first- and second-order polynomial terms.
Use repeated feature encoding to map features to qubits.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on four benchmark functions with varying nonlinearity reports improved performance as ensemble size and individual regressor size increase.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish practical quantum advantage or quantify robustness on noisy quantum hardware.
paper_title: Nonlinear function regression using quantum ensemble learning
